director.name: Dr. Ahmad Kromah
director.quoteTitle: Nurturing the intellect and the soul.
director.quoteP1: Welcome to Yahaya International. When we established this institution in 2020, our goal was simple yet profound: to create an environment where academic rigour meets spiritual depth.
director.quoteP2: We recognised a growing need for an educational model that does not force families to choose between modern excellence and faith-based values. Here, they are seamlessly integrated. Our students are challenged intellectually while being supported emotionally and spiritually.
director.quoteP3: As you explore our community, you will find a dedicated faculty, state-of-the-art facilities, and most importantly, a vibrant student body eager to learn, practise and advocate for a better world.

2020.title: Foundation & First Intake
2020.body: Yahaya International opened its doors with a founding cohort and a simple conviction: that rigorous academics and Islamic character formation belong in the same classroom, not in competition with one another.

2021.title: Curriculum & Faculty Growth
2021.body: We doubled our teaching faculty and completed the integration of the international curriculum with our Qur'anic and Arabic programmes, establishing the dual-track model the school is known for today.

2022.title: Global Accreditation & Leadership Expansion
2022.body: A pivotal year marked by our recognition as a leading global institution. We converged knowledge and faith, cultivating future leaders who advocate for justice, embody empathy, and drive positive change in their communities worldwide.

2023.title: Campus & Facilities Investment
2023.body: New science laboratories, an expanded library and dedicated sports facilities came online, alongside the launch of our online learning platform for students studying beyond the campus.

2024.title: Community & Alumni Network
2024.body: Our first graduating classes moved into universities at home and abroad, and the alumni network was formally established to mentor current students and extend the school's reach into the wider community.

body.p1: The atmosphere at Yahaya International was electric this past week as students from all grades showcased their ingenuity during the 15th Annual Science & Technology Fair.
body.p2: This year's theme, "Sustainability Through Innovation," challenged our young minds to create solutions for real-world environmental issues.
body.p3: From solar-powered water filtration systems to AI-driven waste sorting algorithms, the projects displayed a deep understanding of complex scientific principles. "Our goal is not just to teach science, but to cultivate a mindset of ethical problem-solving," noted Principal Ahmed during his opening address.
body.quote: "Science without conscience is but the ruin of the soul. At Yahaya, we ensure our students understand that every technological advancement must serve humanity and preserve our planet."

list.text: Grade 11 students developed a sensor-based system that reduces campus water usage by 40%.
A competitive category featuring experimental designs for vertical-axis wind turbines.
Yahaya students secured the first position against six regional competitors.

body.p4: As we look forward to the next semester, the school plans to integrate the winning water filtration project into our standard facilities, providing a tangible legacy for this year's participants. We congratulate all students for their hard work and dedication to excellence.

quran-memorization.title: Qur'an Memorization
quran-memorization.desc: Guided Hifz program with tajweed, understanding, and character building — rooted in love for the Qur’an.
quran-memorization.lede: Yahaya International's Qur'an Memorization & Hifz Program offers a scholarly environment where spiritual devotion meets academic rigor, nurturing tomorrow's leaders through the wisdom of the Holy Qur'an.
quran-memorization.pathwayLede: Our Qur’an Memorization program is more than a curriculum; it is a transformative journey. We combine traditional Ottoman and African memorization techniques with modern pedagogical approaches to ensure deep retention and authentic Tajweed.

steps.title: Intensive Memorization
steps.desc: Daily structured sessions focused on new verses, previous revision, and long-term retention.

steps.title: Tafsir & Understanding
steps.desc: Weekly sessions exploring the context and meaning of the memorized portions.

steps.title: Tajweed Mastery
steps.desc: Close attention to articulation and rhythm, corrected one to one with a qualified teacher.

steps.title: Ijazah Pathway
steps.desc: A route to certification for students who complete the programme with consistent excellence.

arabic-immersion.title: Arabic Immersion
arabic-immersion.desc: Comprehensive language acquisition enabling students to engage deeply with classical texts and modern dialogue.
arabic-immersion.lede: A full immersion in classical and modern Arabic, giving students the confidence to read primary sources and hold a conversation with equal ease.
arabic-immersion.pathwayLede: Students move from spoken confidence to classical fluency through daily immersion, structured grammar, and wide reading in original texts.

steps.title: Spoken Foundations
steps.desc: Daily conversation practice that builds fluency before formal grammar takes over.

steps.title: Classical Grammar
steps.desc: Nahw and Sarf taught systematically so that original texts become approachable.

steps.title: Reading Original Texts
steps.desc: Guided study of classical works, read in Arabic from the first term.

steps.title: Composition
steps.desc: Written expression developed through regular assignments and close feedback.

stem-robotics.title: STEM & Robotics
stem-robotics.desc: Hands-on scientific inquiry and programming skills that prepare students for competitive technical fields.
stem-robotics.lede: Laboratory work, programming, and competitive robotics, taught as a single discipline so that theory and practice reinforce one another.
stem-robotics.pathwayLede: From first principles to regional competition, students build, test, and defend their own work throughout the programme.

steps.title: Scientific Method
steps.desc: Enquiry, measurement, and honest reporting established from the first year.

steps.title: Programming
steps.desc: Practical coding taught through problems students actually want to solve.

steps.title: Robotics Build
steps.desc: Design and fabrication in the workshop, culminating in a working machine.

steps.title: Competition
steps.desc: Regional challenges where students present and defend their engineering choices.

islamic-studies.title: Islamic Studies
islamic-studies.desc: In-depth exploration of Fiqh, Aqeedah, and Seerah to build a strong foundational worldview.
islamic-studies.lede: A grounding in Fiqh, Aqeedah, and Seerah that gives students a coherent worldview and the tools to reason within it.
islamic-studies.pathwayLede: Sources are read closely and discussed openly, so that conviction rests on understanding rather than habit.

steps.title: Aqeedah
steps.desc: The foundations of belief, taught with room for genuine questions.

steps.title: Fiqh
steps.desc: Practical jurisprudence applied to the situations students actually meet.

steps.title: Seerah
steps.desc: The Prophetic biography studied as history and as a model of conduct.

steps.title: Ethics in Practice
steps.desc: Character work carried into daily school life, not confined to the classroom.

humanities-arts.title: Humanities & Arts
humanities-arts.desc: Critical thinking through history, literature, and social sciences from global and Islamic perspectives.
humanities-arts.lede: History, literature, and the social sciences read from both global and Islamic perspectives, with argument taken seriously.
humanities-arts.pathwayLede: Students learn to read closely, weigh evidence, and write clearly — the habits that transfer to every other subject.

steps.title: Close Reading
steps.desc: Texts studied slowly and argued over, rather than summarised.

steps.title: Historical Method
steps.desc: Sources weighed for reliability, bias, and context.

steps.title: Written Argument
steps.desc: Essays built on evidence and revised through feedback.

steps.title: Creative Practice
steps.desc: Studio and performance work alongside the written curriculum.

global-leadership.title: Global Leadership
global-leadership.desc: Mentorship, public speaking, and community service projects designed to nurture confident future leaders.
global-leadership.lede: Mentorship, public speaking, and service projects that ask students to lead in front of people who will hold them to it.
global-leadership.pathwayLede: Responsibility is given early and reviewed honestly, so that confidence is earned rather than assumed.

steps.title: Public Speaking
steps.desc: Regular speaking before real audiences, with structured critique.

steps.title: Mentorship
steps.desc: Each student paired with a teacher who follows their progress across years.

steps.title: Service Projects
steps.desc: Community work planned and run by students themselves.

steps.title: Reflection
steps.desc: Written and spoken review of what worked, what did not, and why.

policyModal.contentTerms:
1. Introduction

Welcome to YAHAYA SCHOOL. These Terms and Conditions govern your use of our website and your enrollment in our educational programs. By accessing our website or enrolling, you agree to be bound by these Terms.

2. Admissions and Enrollment

All admissions are subject to review by the YAHAYA SCHOOL administration. We reserve the right to accept or decline any application based on our academic criteria and capacity.

  • Applications must be complete with all required documents.
  • An application fee may apply and is non-refundable.

3. Tuition and Fees

All tuition and fees must be paid in accordance with the schedule provided upon enrollment. Fees are quoted in Liberian Dollars (LRD) or US Dollars (USD).

4. Code of Conduct

Students and parents are expected to adhere to the YAHAYA SCHOOL Code of Conduct. Any behavior that disrupts the educational environment may result in disciplinary action, up to and including expulsion.

5. Intellectual Property

All course materials, website content, and resources provided by YAHAYA SCHOOL are our intellectual property and may not be reproduced or distributed without written permission.

6. Governing Law

These Terms and Conditions shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the Republic of Liberia. Any disputes arising under these Terms shall be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of Liberia.

privacyPage.title: Privacy Policy
privacyPage.content:
1. Information We Collect

We collect personal information that you voluntarily provide to us when you register on the website, express an interest in obtaining information about us or our programs, or otherwise contact us. This includes:

  • Names and contact information (phone numbers, email addresses)
  • Educational history and transcripts
  • Billing and payment information

2. How We Use Your Information

We use personal information collected via our website for a variety of business purposes, including:

  1. Facilitating the enrollment process.
  2. Sending administrative information to you.
  3. Responding to your inquiries and support requests.

3. Information Sharing

We only share information with your consent, to comply with laws, to provide you with services, to protect your rights, or to fulfill business obligations. We do not sell your personal data to third parties.

4. Data Security

We have implemented appropriate technical and organizational security measures designed to protect the security of any personal information we process.

5. Your Privacy Rights

You may review, change, or terminate your account at any time. If you have questions or comments about your privacy rights, you may email us at info@yahayaschool.com.
